'''Zhi-Xun Shen''' ({{zh|s=沈志勋}}; born 1962) is a Chinese-American experimental [[condensed matter physics|condensed matter physicist]]. He is the Paul Pigott Professor of Physical Sciences and a professor of applied physics and of physics at [[Stanford University]], and a senior fellow of Stanford’s [[Precourt Institute for Energy]].<ref name="Stanford">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen's Profile |url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/zhi-xun-shen |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref> He is particularly noted for his [[angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy]] (ARPES) studies on [[high-temperature superconductor]]s. He is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]].<ref name="NAS">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen |url=https://www.nasonline.org/member-directory/members/3007021.html |publisher=National Academy of Sciences |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref><ref name="RoyalSociety">{{cite web |title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/ |publisher=Royal Society |access-date=2026-11-03 |date=2026-05-27}}</ref>

==Life==
Shen was born in 1962 in [[Zhejiang]], China.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://casad.cas.cn/sourcedb_ad_cas/zw2/ysxx/wjysmd/201711/t20171130_4625329.html|title=沈志勋 (Zhixun Shen)|website=Chinese Academy of Sciences|access-date=2019-10-20}}</ref> He graduated from [[Fudan University]] with a B.S. in 1983, and went to the United States through the [[CUSPEA]] program organized by [[T. D. Lee]]. He earned his M.S. degree in 1985 at [[Rutgers University]]. In 1989 he received a PhD in applied physics from [[Stanford University]] under [[Ingolf Lindau]] and [[William E. Spicer]].<ref name="SSRL">{{cite report |title=Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory. Activity report for 1989 |publisher=Stanford Synchrotron Radiation Laboratory |page=126 |url=https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc624243/ |postscript=none}} - via UNT Digital Library.</ref><ref name="AIP">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen |url=https://history.aip.org/phn/11609018.html |publisher=American Institute of Physics |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref> In 1991 he became assistant professor, in 1996 associate professor, and in 2000 full professor at Stanford University.<ref name="AIP" /> At [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]] he was chief scientist from 2010 to 2013 and science and technology advisor from 2013 to 2019.<ref name="Stanford" /> He was the founding director of the Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences (SIMES) from 2006 to 2011.<ref name="Stanford" /><ref name="Radcliffe">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen |url=https://www.radcliffe.harvard.edu/people/zhi-xun-shen |publisher=Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study, Harvard University |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref> Furthermore, from 2005 to 2008 he was director of the [[Geballe Laboratory for Advanced Materials]].<ref name="AIP" /> He has held the Paul Pigott Professorship in Physical Sciences since 2006 and is a senior fellow of Stanford’s Precourt Institute for Energy.<ref name="Stanford" />

==Research==
Shen’s group uses angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy and other photon-based techniques, including soft X-ray scattering and time- and spin-resolved spectroscopy, to study quantum materials such as superconductors, magnets and topological insulators.<ref name="ShenLab">{{cite web |title=Shen Laboratory |url=https://arpes.stanford.edu/ |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref>

In 1993, Shen and co-workers reported a strongly anisotropic superconducting gap in Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> (Bi2212), consistent with d-wave pairing.<ref name="paper1">{{cite journal |author=Z.-X. Shen |display-authors=etal |title=Anomalously large gap anisotropy in the a-b plane of Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=70 |pages=((1553-1556)) |year=1993 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.70.1553}}</ref>

Over the following decade, Shen and collaborators traced how the electronic structure of a strongly correlated Mott insulator evolves with carrier doping into anomalous metallic and superconducting states. Their studies progressed from measurements of band dispersion in undoped cuprates and electronic reorganization upon doping, published in 1995,<ref name="paper5">{{cite journal |author=B. O. Wells |display-authors=etal |title=E versus k Relations and Many Body Effects in the Model Insulating Copper Oxide Sr<sub>2</sub>CuO<sub>2</sub>Cl<sub>2</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=74 |pages=((964-967)) |year=1995 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.74.964}}</ref><ref name="paper6">{{cite journal |author=D. M. King |display-authors=etal |title=Electronic structure evolution from Mott insulator to superconductor-An angle-resolved photoemission investigation |journal=Journal of Physics and Chemistry of Solids |volume=56 |pages=((1865-1869)) |year=1995 |doi=10.1016/0022-3697(95)00262-6}}</ref> to the identification in 1996 of a momentum-dependent normal-state excitation gap in underdoped samples, leaving only a segment of the Fermi surface, now known as the pseudogap and Fermi arc.<ref name="paper7">{{cite journal |author=D. S. Marshall |display-authors=etal |title=Unconventional Electronic Structure Evolution with Hole Doping in Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub>: Angle-Resolved Photoemission Results |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=76 |pages=((4841-4844)) |year=1996 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.4841}}</ref><ref name="paper8">{{cite journal |author=A. G. Loeser |display-authors=etal |title=Excitation Gap in the Normal State of Underdoped Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>CaCu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> |journal=Science |volume=273 |pages=((325-329)) |year=1996 |doi=10.1126/science.273.5273.325}}</ref>

Beginning in 2001, Shen’s group also reported evidence for strong electron-phonon coupling in cuprates.<ref name="paper12">{{cite journal |author=A. Lanzara |display-authors=etal |title=Evidence for ubiquitous strong electron-phonon coupling in high-temperature superconductors |journal=Nature |volume=412 |pages=((510-514)) |year=2001 |doi=10.1038/35087518}}</ref> In 2004, they identified coupling between electrons and the B<sub>1g</sub> oxygen-buckling phonon in the antinodal regions of Bi2212, where the superconducting gap is largest.<ref name="paper13">{{cite journal |author=T. Cuk |display-authors=etal |title=Coupling of the B<sub>1g</sub> Phonon to the Antinodal Electronic States of Bi<sub>2</sub>Sr<sub>2</sub>Ca<sub>0.92</sub>Y<sub>0.08</sub>Cu<sub>2</sub>O<sub>8+δ</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=93 |article-number=117003 |year=2004 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.93.117003}}</ref> In 2018, they reported evidence suggesting that electron-phonon coupling and electronic correlations act cooperatively to enhance superconductivity.<ref name="paper14">{{cite journal |author=Y. He |display-authors=etal |title=Rapid change of superconductivity and electron-phonon coupling through critical doping in Bi-2212 |journal=Science |volume=362 |pages=((62-65)) |year=2018 |doi=10.1126/science.aar3394}}</ref> Studies of doped one-dimensional cuprates further elucidated the interplay between electron-phonon coupling and Mott physics.<ref name="paper15">{{cite journal |author=Z. Chen |display-authors=etal |title=Anomalously strong near-neighbor attraction in doped 1D cuprate chains |journal=Science |volume=373 |pages=((1235-1239)) |year=2021 |doi=10.1126/science.abf5174}}</ref><ref name="paper16">{{cite journal |author=Y. Wang |display-authors=etal |title=Phonon-Mediated Long-Range Attractive Interaction in One-Dimensional Cuprates |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=127 |article-number=197003 |year=2021 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.127.197003}}</ref>

His group’s measurements of Sr<sub>2</sub>RuO<sub>4</sub> and Sr<sub>2</sub>RhO<sub>4</sub> demonstrated quantitative agreement with bulk electronic and thermodynamic properties.<ref name="paper18">{{cite journal |author=A. Damascelli |display-authors=etal |title=Fermi Surface, Surface States, and Surface Reconstruction in Sr<sub>2</sub>RuO<sub>4</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=85 |pages=((5194-5197)) |year=2000 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.85.5194}}</ref><ref name="paper19">{{cite journal |author=F. Baumberger |display-authors=etal |title=Fermi Surface and Quasiparticle Excitations of Sr<sub>2</sub>RhO<sub>4</sub> |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=96 |article-number=246402 |year=2006 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.246402}}</ref> In 2022, the group further established a connection between ARPES measurements and thermodynamic properties in cuprates.<ref name="paper20">{{cite journal |author=S.-D. Chen |display-authors=etal |title=Unconventional spectral signature of Tc in a pure d-wave superconductor |journal=Nature |volume=601 |pages=((562-567)) |year=2022 |doi=10.1038/s41586-021-04251-2}}</ref>

Shen and collaborators extended these methods to a broader range of quantum materials, including iron-based superconductors, correlated oxides, topological insulators and low-dimensional systems. In 2009, they experimentally identified Bi<sub>2</sub>Te<sub>3</sub> as a three-dimensional topological insulator with a single surface Dirac cone.<ref name="paper21">{{cite journal |author=Y. L. Chen |display-authors=etal |title=Experimental Realization of a Three-Dimensional Topological Insulator, Bi<sub>2</sub>Te<sub>3</sub> |journal=Science |volume=325 |pages=((178-181)) |year=2009 |doi=10.1126/science.1173034}}</ref> In 2017, they reported evidence for a quantum spin Hall state in monolayer 1T′-WTe<sub>2</sub>.<ref name="paper22">{{cite journal |author=S. Tang |display-authors=etal |title=Quantum spin Hall state in monolayer 1T′-WTe<sub>2</sub> |journal=Nature Physics |volume=13 |pages=((683-687)) |year=2017 |doi=10.1038/nphys4174}}</ref> Their work also explored the interplay between lattice vibrations and electronic correlations. In 2014, the group reported evidence that coupling to phonons in the SrTiO<sub>3</sub> substrate substantially enhances superconductivity in monolayer FeSe.<ref name="paper23">{{cite journal |author=J. J. Lee |display-authors=etal |title=Interfacial mode coupling as the origin of the enhancement of Tc in FeSe films on SrTiO<sub>3</sub> |journal=Nature |volume=515 |pages=((245-248)) |year=2014 |doi=10.1038/nature13894}}</ref> In 2017, combined time-resolved photoemission and X-ray diffraction measurements quantified electron-phonon coupling in FeSe and demonstrated its enhancement by electronic correlations.<ref name="paper24">{{cite journal |author=S. Gerber |display-authors=etal |title=Femtosecond electron-phonon lock-in by photoemission and x-ray free-electron laser |journal=Science |volume=357 |pages=((71-74)) |year=2017 |doi=10.1126/science.aak9946}}</ref>

Shen’s group also developed cantilever-based scanning microwave impedance microscopy, a near-field technique for imaging local electrical properties at the nanoscale.<ref name="paper25">{{cite journal |author1=K. Lai |author2=W. Kundhikanjana |author3=M. A. Kelly |author4=Z.-X. Shen |title=Modeling and characterization of a cantilever-based near-field scanning microwave impedance microscope |journal=Review of Scientific Instruments |volume=79 |article-number=063703 |year=2008 |doi=10.1063/1.2949109}}</ref> He co-authored the 2010 proposal of photon-enhanced thermionic emission for concentrated solar-energy conversion.<ref name="paper26">{{cite journal |author=J. W. Schwede |display-authors=etal |title=Photon-enhanced thermionic emission for solar concentrator systems |journal=Nature Materials |volume=9 |pages=((762-767)) |year=2010 |doi=10.1038/nmat2814}}</ref>

Shen has trained numerous graduate students and postdoctoral researchers who have gone on to lead independent research groups at universities and research institutions worldwide.<ref name="StanfordFRS">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen elected to Royal Society |url=https://humsci.stanford.edu/feature/zhi-xun-shen-elected-royal-society |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2026-11-03 |last=Zaske |first=Sara |date=2026-06-02}}</ref>

==Honors==
* 1993: [[Sloan Research Fellowship]]<ref name="Stanford" />
* 1994: Outstanding Scientific Accomplishment Award, DOE Office of Basic Energy Sciences<ref name="Stanford" />
* 1999: American Physical Society Centennial Lecturer<ref name="Stanford" />
* 2000: [[Kamerlingh Onnes Prize]]<ref name="Stanford" />
* 2002: Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name="AIP" />
* 2009: [[Ernest Orlando Lawrence Award]]<ref name="Lawrence">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen, 2009 |url=https://science.osti.gov/lawrence/Award-Laureates/2000s/shen |publisher=U.S. Department of Energy |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref>
* 2011: [[Oliver E. Buckley Condensed Matter Prize]], together with [[Juan Carlos Campuzano]] and Peter Johnson<ref name="Buckley">{{cite web |title=Brookhaven Scientist Peter Johnson Shares American Physical Society Oliver E. Buckley Prize |url=https://www.bnl.gov/newsroom/news.php?a=111199 |publisher=Brookhaven National Laboratory |access-date=2026-11-03 |last=Yuhas |first=Daisy |date=2010-12-02}}</ref>
* 2014: Investigator, Emerging Phenomena in Quantum Systems initiative, [[Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation]]<ref name="Stanford" /><ref name="Moore">{{cite web |title=Professors Aharon Kapitulnik, Zhi-Xun Shen and Tony Heinz receive Moore Foundation Awards in Quantum Materials |url=https://physics.stanford.edu/news/professors-aharon-kapitulnik-zhi-xun-shen-and-tony-heinz-receive-moore-foundation-awards |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2026-11-03 |date=2014-11-11}}</ref>
* 2015: Member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="NAS" />
* 2017: Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]; foreign member of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]<ref name="AAAS">{{cite web |title=Zhi-Xun Shen elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences |url=https://physics.stanford.edu/news/zhi-xun-shen-elected-american-academy-arts-and-sciences |publisher=Stanford University |access-date=2026-11-03 |date=2017-04-12}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.casad.ac.cn/doc/17503.html|title=关于公布2017年中国科学院院士增选当选院士名单的公告|date=2017-11-28|publisher=Chinese Academy of Sciences|language=zh|access-date=2018-06-17|archive-date=2017-12-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171202014847/http://www.casad.ac.cn/doc/17503.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2019-2020: William and Flora Hewlett Foundation Fellow, [[Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study]]<ref name="Radcliffe" />
* 2020: Tage Erlander Guest Professorship, [[Swedish Research Council]] and [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]]<ref name="Erlander">{{cite web |title=Installation of the 2020 holder of the Tage Erlander Visiting Professorship |url=https://www.vr.se/english/just-now/events/event-archive/2020-03-09-installation-of-the-2020-holder-of-the-tage-erlander-visiting-professorship.html |publisher=Swedish Research Council |access-date=2026-11-03}}</ref>
* 2026: [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name="RoyalSociety" />
